subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm sorry, I don't have that information on hand, but I can tell you that I've been struggling with my asthma for the past six months, and it's been really frustrating because I seem to have flare-ups almost every month or every other month. I've been going to urgent care and my primary care doctor quite a bit, and sometimes they give me antibiotics or steroids. I really need help getting this under control so I can start enjoying things like hiking again. Doctor: Could you please provide your age, gender, and occupation? Patient: I'm not sure about my exact age, but I'm an adult. I'm female, and I work a regular office job. I don't have any specific issues with my job that seem to trigger my asthma. Doctor: Could you please provide details about any previous asthma diagnosis, medications you have been prescribed, and whether you have undergone any pulmonary function tests or imaging studies? Patient: I was told during my last visit that I have asthma, and I'm currently using a blue inhaler called Ventolin, which I use almost every day because I'm always coughing and wheezing. I also use it a couple of times a week at night when I wake up needing relief. I was given a pulmonary function test during my last office visit, and the results were consistent with asthma. I haven't had any imaging studies done for my asthma. Doctor: Could you please describe any specific triggers or situations that seem to worsen your asthma symptoms, such as allergens, exercise, or changes in weather? Additionally, have you noticed any patterns in your symptoms, such as worsening during certain times of the day or week? Patient: I find that my asthma flares up a lot when I get sick with a cold, and I think my aunt's cat might be a trigger too. I try to avoid going there now. My symptoms seem to happen almost every month or every other month, and I usually end up needing my inhaler almost every day, especially at night a couple of times
